name: Bangkok
literature_vertical_cm_per_yr: 0.5 to 1.0 in inner Bangkok; 1 to 3 in eastern/suburban industrial districts (historical 1980s peak 10 to 12)
literature_sources: Phien-wej, N., Giao, P.H., & Nutalaya, P. (2006), Engineering Geology
Aobpaet, A. et al. (2013), InSAR time-series analysis of land subsidence in Bangkok, Thailand
agreement_note: 120-day monsoon-season LOS peak (-7.5 cm LOS; -9.0 cm vertical est.) is 7-10x larger than modern published InSAR rates (1-3 cm/yr in outer districts). Valid pixel fraction is 34.6% (<40% high-confidence threshold) with only 2 references; tropical wet-delay atmospheric turbulence during June-October monsoon acquisitions likely inflates the short-window amplitude.
press_summary_gate_note: Exclude headline rate from press summary; retain as indicative-only due to monsoon atmospheric noise, 34.6% valid pixels, and 7-10x discrepancy vs. modern literature.

first_nisar_measurement.evidence: No peer-reviewed or official NASA/ISRO NISAR subsidence publication found for Bangkok as of 2026-11-14.

quality_note: NISAR data are provisional. Calibration and validation are carried out by the NISAR project (NASA-JPL and ISRO), not by our team.
